RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Wednesday, December 19, 2018/Agrahayana 28, 1940 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Civil Aviation; Commerce and Industry; Home Affairs; Labour and
Employment; Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises; Petroleum and Natural
Gas; Skill Development and Entrepreneurship; Steel; Textiles)
Total number of questions — 15
31
Air connectivity in West Bengal under
UDAN scheme
*91. SHRI SUKHENDU SEKHAR
RAY: Will the Minister of CIVIL
A VIATION be pleased to state:
(a) how many cities/towns in West
Bengal have been included in the UDAN
scheme to facilitate air connectivity;
(b) what steps Government have
initiated to connect Cooch Behar,
Balurghat and Malda by air, where
functional airstrips already exist, the details
thereof;
(c) whether Government has any plan
to introduce direct round trip Air India
flights from International Airport, Kolkata
to the capitals of island countries like
Singapore, Maldives, Indonesia, Malaysia,
Philippines, Sri Lanka etc. for promoting
tourism in Eastern India; and
(d) if so, by when and if not, the reasons
therefor?
Underpaid jobs under skill
development
*92. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: Will
the Minister of LABOUR AND
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that not even 50
per cent of the total number of trained
persons under skill development in various
Ministries got jobs;
(b) whether it is also a fact that private
employees and job seekers are getting
underpaid jobs, which is the burning issue
in the unemployment sector; and
(c) the status of promise made by the
Prime Minister to give one crore good jobs?
MSME Conclave in Guwahati
*93. SHRI BHUBANESWAR
KALITA: Will the Minister of MICRO,
SMALL  AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES
be pleased to state:
(a) whether North East Micro, Small
and Medium Enterprises (MSME)

32
Conclave was held in January, 2018 in
Guwahati and if so, the details thereof;
(b) whether MSME sector is a critical
component to India's growth story;
(c) whether Government would also
agree that MSME sector is also making
significant contribution to GDP,
employment and exports; and
(d) if so, the details thereof along with
the initiatives taken by Government to
strengthen the sector in Assam?
Central funding for projects in
naxalite affected areas
*94. SHRIMATI SHANTA  CHHETRI:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Integrated
Action Plan (IAP) for broad co-ordinated
operations aimed at dealing with the
naxalite problem in all the affected States
including West Bengal have borne positive
results;
(b) if so, the details of  Central funding
for grassroot economic development
projects in naxalite affected areas; and
(c) whether there has been an increased
special police funding for better
containment and reduction of naxalite
influence?
Industrial Park Rating System
*95. DR. VIKAS MAHATME: Will the
Minister of  COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) the criteria that was used by
Government in the recently released
'Industrial Park Rating System' to assess
the quality of infrastructure in industrial
parks, the details thereof;
(b) the number of industrial parks that
were assessed in this exercise and their
distribution, State/UT-wise;
(c) whether this system will help India
in entering into the top 50 countries in the
Ease of Doing Business Index; and
(d) further steps, if any, proposed to be
taken to make it easier for policy makers
and investors to gauge the infrastructure
services at an industrial park?
Setting up of large scale PNG network
*96. DR. AMEE Y AJNIK: Will the
Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has any
proposal to set up Piped Natural Gas (PNG)
network on a large scale in near future;
(b) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasosn therefor; and
(c)  the details about the plan outlay
and nodal agencies regarding the
aforementioned plan?
Attacks on RTI workers, whistle
blowers and social workers
*97. SHRIMATI JHARNA DAS
BAIDYA: Will the Minister of HOME
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) the number of attacks that took place
on RTI workers, whistle blowers and social
workers during the last three years, the
details thereof;
(b) whether NCRB classify these
attacks in a different head, if so, the details
of the attacks during the last three years as
reported by NCRB, if not, the reasons
therefor; and
(c) in how many cases FIRs have been
registered, chargesheets filed, trials and

33
convictions/acquittals from 2015 onwards,
the data thereof?
Cardamom imports from Sri Lanka
*98. SHRI K.K. RAGESH: Will the
Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether the improts of cardamom
from Sri Lanka to India is increasing;
(b) if so, the month-wise details of such
cardamom imports from Sri Lanka during
the last six months;
(c) whether Government is in receipt
of any complaints about the dubious
financial dealings involved in such
increased import

List of Questions for WRITTEN ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Wednesday, December 19, 2018/Agrahayana 28, 1940 (Saka)

(Ministries : Civil Aviation; Commerce and Industry; Home Affairs; Labour and
Employment; Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises; Petroleum and Natural
Gas; Skill Development and Entrepreneurship; Steel; Textiles)
Total number of questions — 160
223
Safety measures and programmes  for
airliners
961. SHRIMATI VIPLOVE
THAKUR: Will the Minister of CIVIL
A VIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has chalked
out any safety measure and programme to
enhance and ensure safety of airliners;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government has taken any
serious note of old aircraft being operated
by certain airlines; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and the
reaction of Government thereto?
Foreign pilots employed by various
airlines in the country
962. SHRIMATI VIPLOVE
THAKUR: Will the Minister of CIVIL
A VIATION be pleased to state:
(a) the total number of foreign pilots
employed by various airlines in the country,
airline-wise;
(b) whether the aviation industry is
witnessing any stagnation in terms of
opportunities to Indian pilots to enhance
their training skills;
(c) if so, the details thereof and the steps
taken by Government to replace foreign
pilots with Indian pilots;
(d) whether Government has assessed
the requirement of pilots in the country, if
so, the details thereof and the measures
taken by Government in this regard; and
(e) the anticipated time-frame by when
all the trained foreign pilots of scheduled
carriers would finally be repatriated?
Regional Connectivity Scheme to
promote civil aviation
963. SHRI OSCAR FERNANDES:
Will the Minister of CIVIL A VIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has any
proposal to include some nearby centres
of Delhi/NCR/Rajasthan and Maharashtra
in Regional Connectivity Scheme to
promote the aviation industry;

224
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and
(d) the details of the plan outlay
regarding the inclusion of urban centres in
the aforesaid scheme which already has a
long air strip?
Arbitrary increase of fare by private
airlines
†964. SHRI SURENDRA SINGH
NAGAR: Will the Minister of CIVIL
A VIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that private
airlines increase their fares arbitrarily
because there is no monitoring mechanism
by Government in place;
(b) if so, reasons for not bringing the
operations of private airlines and their fare
determination policy under any regulatory
commission so far; and
(c) if not, what steps Government takes
to monitor the fares and other matters
relating to the private airlines?
Upgradation of Bagdogra
airport
965. SHRIMATI SHANTA CHHETRI:
Will the Minister of CIVIL A VIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether steps are being taken to
upgrade Bagdogra airport which is the
gateway to Darjeeling, North Bengal and
Bhutan; and
(b) whether any policy and programme
has been taken to increase the frequency
of flights due to steady rise in demand from
major cities such as Kolkata, Delhi,
Mumbai, Chennai, etc.?
Complaints lodged by passengers
against Air India
966. SHRI T. RATHINA VEL: Will the
Minister of CIVIL A VIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Air India
had the most number of complaints lodged
against it by passengers;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that various
reasons for complaints were due to flight
problem followed by baggage issues and
customer service;
(d) whether it is also a fact that staff
behaviour, refund fare, disability and
catering were the other reasons why
passengers had lodged complaints; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Extra fees charged by private airlines
for seats
†967. SHRIMATI CHHAYA
VERMA:
SHRI VISHAMBHAR
PRASAD NISHAD:
CH. SUKHRAM SINGH
YADA V:
Will the Minister of CIVIL A VIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether  the private airlines are
charging extra fees from passengers for seat
selection and fixing fees for all seats during
web check-in which the passengers are
bound to pay;
(b) whether  the Ministry  is showing
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

225
laxity in following rules due to which the
airlines are charging such fees from the
passengers in an arbitrary manner;
(c) details of action taken against the
airlines during the last three years for
ignoring complaints and flouting rules;
and
(d) whether Government will review the
matter regarding system of seat selection
fees so that the passengers do not have to
pay extra charges?
Policy for flying drones
968. SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has finalized
policy for regulation for flying drones in
the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether registration is required for
flying drones including nano drones;
(d) whether safety aspects including
security interests were kept
